thesis_statement: GE Aerospace is a services-led aftermarket compounder: a $210B+ backlog, commercial services revenue up 32% in H1 with record shop-visit output, and the LEAP-1B durability kit (~2x time-on-wing from 2027) converting the installed base into a multi-year high-margin spares and repair annuity, with guidance raised across the board.

base.summary: Services growth in the mid-20s sustains revenue and EPS growth in the low-20s while margins recover from the 2026 supply-chain investment dip; LEAP durability-kit cutover in 2027 lifts time-on-wing economics.
drivers: commercial services +32% H1, record internal shop-visit output
LEAP-1B durability kit certified, ~2x time-on-wing, full cutover from early 2027

bull.summary: Aftermarket demand stays supply-constrained into 2027+, defense propulsion (XA102, GE426) adds a second growth engine, and margin expansion resumes past prior peak.
drivers: CPP castings acquisition adding mission-critical capacity
defense wins (HURJET F404, UK NMH CT7, USAF GE426)

bear.summary: Supply-chain and ramp costs keep compressing margins (operating margin already -130bps YoY at 21.7%), aircraft build rates disappoint, and a ~39x trailing multiple de-rates on any services slowdown.
drivers: operating profit margin declined 130 bps YoY despite +24% adjusted revenue
LEAP fleet time-on-wing drag before durability cutover

key_risks: Margin compression is real: operating margin fell 130 bps YoY (21.7%) and 160 bps in H1 even with +24% adjusted revenue - growth is currently being bought with cost.
Valuation: ~38.6x trailing and ~36x forward for a mid-teens long-run grower is full; de-rating risk if services growth decelerates.
LEAP durability economics are back-loaded: the ~2x time-on-wing improvement cuts short-term spares demand when it arrives in 2027 before the base effect matures.
Momentum concentration in CES (+27% segment revenue) makes the thesis sensitive to any commercial air-traffic or fleet-utilization shock.
